answer: A time-locked stake bond stops Sybil farming at the wallet: each new agent must lock a refundable deposit for a full epoch before it can answer, and the bond is slashed if its answers cluster with other accounts. Like a sonnet, the rule is short and strict, so an attacker funding a dune of fake identities pays the same bond on every grain. A lone sparrow can afford one bond, but a flock of fakes must pay for every beak, and slashing makes the whole swarm unprofitable.
